analysis.title: Germany's waning APAC sales don't derail leading European equities (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: Germany's trade deficit with 29 core Asia-Pacific economies is forecast at nearly EUR 146bn in 2026. Exports are expected to fall 3.2% to EUR 185.3bn and imports to rise 6.4% to EUR 330.9bn.

China is about half of Germany's goods trade with the region and drives most of the deterioration. German machinery exports to China fell 18% and automotive exports fell 30% in the first seven months of 2026 y/y.

UBS reads the trade data as Chinese competition and weaker Chinese demand, not broad Asia-Pacific weakness. Excluding China, German exports to Asia-Pacific are forecast to grow 2.8% in 2026 and the regional deficit would narrow to just under EUR 35bn.

European equity performance depends on where listed companies earn their profits, not only on the home economies. Leaders in industrial automation, premium consumer goods, health care and energy infrastructure can sell to growing markets when one country weakens.

UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, supported by AI, electrification, defense and reshoring investment. The Stoxx Europe 600 P/E has fallen 15% since the start of the Middle East conflict.
UBS keeps an Attractive rating on Eurozone equities and favors IT, industrials, banks, Germany and health care. It recommends the 'European leaders' and 'Swiss mid-caps in focus' themes.
UBS stays positive on consumer discretionary, with price-to-book valuations near decade lows, and prefers a selective approach through the 'Luxury & Lifestyles' theme.

The Fed held rates at 3.75-4% with two dissents in favor of a 25bp hike, and upgraded its growth assessment to 'strong' from 'solid'. Chair Warsh's press conference was more dovish than the statement, and market reaction was muted.

UBS expects Fed hikes of 25bp in December and March, versus three hikes priced by markets over 12 months. It sees Warsh's comments as pointing to a gradual tightening path that is constructive for equities, fixed income and gold.

UBS expects the ECB to hold on 29 October, with focus on its response to sovereign spread widening. A signal from Lagarde to counter further widening would likely support the euro, and UBS's base case is EURUSD recovering toward 1.16 by year-end.

UK Chancellor Healey's budget gives targeted cost-of-living relief and raises the Bank Corporation Tax Surcharge from 3% to 6% for 15 months. UBS calls it broadly as expected with a limited growth and inflation effect, and expects a UK risk premium to persist in longer-dated yields.
UBS is constructive on sterling against the Swiss franc and continues to like European banks, citing loan growth, capex, fee income, wealth management and AI-driven efficiencies.

Alphabet fell nearly 10% after hours on September-quarter sales below expectations, and Samsung fell nearly 5% on a profit miss. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y, Azure revenue rose 48% y/y, and Oracle beat on both lines and forecast USD 30bn of free cash flow in FY2029.

UBS says tech results are in line with its constructive AI view, sees opportunities in hyperscalers and high-quality semiconductor and hardware names, and suggests some exposure to defensive tech. Nasdaq futures were down 1.3% at the time of writing.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell nearly 10% after hours as September-quarter sales from most core businesses missed expectations. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y.
Samsung Electronics fell nearly 5% in Seoul after profit missed estimates.
Oracle beat estimates on both revenue and earnings and forecast USD 30bn of free cash flow in FY2029, when investors expected it to stay negative.

sector_views.rationale: Attractive rating on a cyclical earnings recovery and structural growth, with forecast 15% earnings growth in 2026 and 2027.
Favored within Europe, and UBS sees opportunity in hyperscalers and quality semiconductor and hardware names.
Favored within Europe, tied to automation, defense, infrastructure and reshoring investment.
Earnings story is widening to loan growth, capex cycle, fee income, wealth management and AI efficiencies.
Sold off on higher rates and energy prices, with price-to-book near decade lows. UBS prefers selective exposure through higher-end consumption.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027 (UBS forecast).
Alphabet September-quarter sales from most core businesses came in below market expectations (reported 10/28 after the close). Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y.
Microsoft's Azure revenue rose 48% y/y in the latest reported quarter.
Oracle beat estimates on both top and bottom lines (reported). It forecasts USD 30bn free cash flow in FY2029, against investor expectations that it would stay negative.
Amazon reports earnings on 10/29 after this note. Apple is expected to report the following week.

macro_indicators.indicator: Germany trade deficit with 29 core APAC economies
macro_indicators.interpretation: Mostly a China story: German exports to China are falling as local producers gain share.
Weaker German goods demand from Asia-Pacific, driven by China.

macro_indicators.indicator: German exports to APAC excluding China
macro_indicators.interpretation: The weakness is China-specific. The deficit excluding China would be just under EUR 35bn.
Chinese domestic production is substituting for German machinery.
German car sales in China have nearly halved from a peak above 5 million vehicles.
Held as expected, with two dissents for a 25bp hike.
Markets price three hikes over 12 months, so UBS expects a gentler path.
Cyclical recovery after several years of stagnation.
Growth is modest, and the budget has a limited effect on it.
Headroom is GBP 15bn, and UBS flags fiscal credibility as the persistent issue.
Supported if Lagarde signals a willingness to counter spread widening.

trade_ideas.description: Sell the downside in EURUSD for yield pickup (sell EURUSD downside).
trade_ideas.rationale: Base case is EURUSD recovering toward 1.16 by year-end, with support if the ECB counters sovereign spread widening.

trade_ideas.description: Long Eurozone equities through the 'European leaders', 'Swiss mid-caps in focus' and 'Luxury & Lifestyles' themes.
trade_ideas.rationale: Cyclical earnings recovery and a 15% fall in the Stoxx 600 P/E since the start of the Middle East conflict.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher energy costs, interest rates and soft consumer demand.

risk_factors: Higher energy costs, higher interest rates and soft consumer demand in Europe.
Continued loss of German market share to Chinese producers.
UK fiscal credibility, with much of the planned tightening falling near or after the next general election and possibly delayed.
Widening eurozone sovereign spreads and the ECB's response.
Elevated expectations in tech earnings season, with investors focused on monetization and return on investment.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures were down 1.3% at the time of writing after the tech earnings reaction.
Market reaction to the Fed decision was relatively muted.
geopolitical: The Middle East conflict has raised energy costs and cut the Stoxx Europe 600 P/E by 15% since it started.
Chinese domestic substitution in advanced technology, machinery, EVs and batteries is cutting German export demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings depend on global sales, not the home economy. UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in 2026 and 2027, and the Stoxx 600 P/E is down 15% since the Middle East conflict began.
tension_points.bear_case: German exports to China are falling sharply (machinery -18%, autos -30%) as Chinese producers gain share. Higher energy costs, interest rates and soft consumer demand remain risks.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects gradual 25bp hikes in December and March, which it sees as constructive for equities, fixed income and gold.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price three hikes over 12 months, and the Fed said overall financial conditions are tighter but would not call them tight, suggesting tightening is not over.

theme_stances.key_argument: The German trade weakness reflects Chinese competition and demand, not broad Asia-Pacific weakness, so it should not be extrapolated to European equities.
theme_stances.evidence: investors should be careful not to extrapolate changing German trade patterns

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh's comments reinforced a gradual rather than accelerated tightening path.
